chapters.title: Ch 1 · Software engineering practices and ethics

sources.title: Chapter 5: Requirements Engineering & System Modeling Quiz

questions.q: What is software?
questions.e: Software includes computer programs and all associated documentation such as requirements, design models, and user manuals.

questions.q: One of the following is NOT an attribute of good software:
questions.e: Unpredictability is NOT a desirable attribute. Good software should be predictable, maintainable, dependable, and efficient.

questions.q: What is software validation?
o: Checking that the software is free from bugs
Ensuring the software meets customer requirements
questions.e: Validation answers "Are we building the right product?" - ensuring the software meets the customer's actual needs and expectations.

questions.q: What is the primary focus of software engineering?
questions.e: Software engineering is concerned with ALL aspects of software production from initial conception through to maintaining the system after it has gone into use.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the fundamental software engineering activities?
questions.e: The four fundamental activities are: Specification, Development, Validation, and Evolution. Marketing is not a fundamental software engineering activity.

questions.q: Roughly what percentage of software costs are development costs?
questions.e: Roughly 60% of software costs are development costs, and 40% are testing costs. For custom software, evolution costs often exceed development costs.

questions.q: Software does not deteriorate over time; "it wears out".
questions.e: Software does NOT wear out like hardware. However, it DOES deteriorate over time due to changing requirements, environments, and poor maintenance practices.

questions.q: Generic products specification is owned by:
questions.e: In generic products (like MS Office), the specification is owned by the software developer. In customized products, the customer owns the specification.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a generic product?
o: Embedded control system for a car
questions.e: Microsoft Word is a generic product sold to the general market. The others are customized products developed for specific customers or purposes.

questions.q: What does the "Commodity" attribute of good software design mean?
o: A program should not have any bugs that inhibit its function
A program should be suitable for the purposes for which it was intended
The experience of using the program should be pleasurable
A program should not have any inconsistencies or omissions
questions.e: According to Mitch Kapor's software design manifesto, Commodity means the program should be suitable for its intended purposes.

questions.q: Which is a key challenge faced by software engineering?
questions.e: Key challenges include: heterogeneity/diversity, business and social change, security and trust, and scale.

questions.q: List and briefly explain the four essential attributes of good software.
questions.m:
Model Answer:
The four essential attributes are: Maintainability: Software should be written so it can evolve to meet changing customer needs Dependability: Includes reliability, security, and safety. The software should not cause physical or economic damage Efficiency: Software should not waste system resources such as memory and processor cycles Acceptability/Usability: Software must be understandable, usable, and compatible with other systems

questions.q: Explain why software engineers should adhere to a professional code of ethics. List at least three principles from the ACM/IEEE Code of Ethics.
questions.m:
Model Answer:
Software engineers should adhere to ethical codes because: Software has a central role in society and can cause significant harm if misused Engineers have opportunities to do good or cause harm Professional behavior builds trust with customers and society Three ACM/IEEE principles: PUBLIC: Act consistently with the public interest CLIENT AND EMPLOYER: Act in the best interests of client and employer, consistent with public interest PRODUCT: Ensure products meet highest professional standards JUDGMENT: Maintain integrity and independence in professional judgment

questions.q: (2 points) The Project Management Spectrum focuses on the four P's. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.e: The four P's are: People, Product, Process, and Project. Performance is not one of them.

questions.q: (2 points) Which of the following is NOT a key stakeholder type in software projects?
questions.e: Competitors are not considered stakeholders in a software project. Stakeholders include senior managers, project managers, practitioners, customers, and end-users.

questions.q: (2 points) A team leader needs to develop three key skills. Which of the following is one of them?
questions.e: The three key skills for a team leader are: Motivation, Organization, and Ideas/Innovation.

questions.q: (2 points) What does high "Fan-out" for a function indicate?
o: The function is loosely coupled with the rest of the design
The function is tightly coupled with the rest of the design
questions.e: High Fan-out means the function is tightly coupled with the rest of the design because it calls many other functions. This indicates high complexity and dependency.

questions.q: (2 points) In risk management, which strategy aims to reduce the probability that a risk will arise?
questions.e: Avoidance strategy reduces the probability that a risk will arise. Minimization reduces the impact, and contingency planning prepares for when risks occur.

questions.q: (2 points) According to the triple constraints for software projects, which three factors must be balanced?
questions.e: The triple constraints (also called the project management triangle) are Quality, Cost, and Time. Any change in one affects the others.

questions.q: (2 points) In the Critical Path Method (CPM), what is "Total Slack"?
o: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the project completion
The shortest path through the network
The number of resources assigned to a task
questions.e: Total Slack (or Total Float) is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the project completion date. It's calculated as LS - ES or LF - EF.

questions.q: (2 points) Which risk type relates to "staff turnover"?
questions.e: Staff turnover is a Project risk because it affects the project schedule and resources directly.

questions.q: (1 point) The Critical Path is the shortest path through a project network diagram.
questions.e: FALSE: The Critical Path is the LONGEST path through a project network diagram, not the shortest. It determines the minimum project duration.

questions.q: (1 point) Risk monitoring should be done only at the beginning of the project.
questions.e: FALSE: Risk monitoring should be done regularly throughout the entire project lifecycle, not just at the beginning. Risks should be assessed at management progress meetings.

questions.q: (1 point) In agile teams, self-organizing teams make their own decisions about project management and technical matters.
questions.e: TRUE: In agile teams, self-organizing teams are given autonomy to make their own project management and technical decisions to get the job done.

questions.q: (1 point) The Early Finish (EF) of a task is calculated as: EF = ES + Duration
questions.e: TRUE: Early Finish is calculated by adding the task duration to the Early Start: EF = ES + Duration.

questions.q: (2 points) What is the primary purpose of requirements engineering?
o: To write code for the system
To establish the services the customer requires and constraints under which it operates
To test the system after deployment
questions.e: Requirements engineering establishes the services the customer requires from a system and the constraints under which it operates and is developed.

questions.q: (2 points) Which of the following is a functional requirement?
o: The system shall be available 99.9% of the time
The system shall generate a daily report of patient appointments
The system shall respond within 2 seconds
The system shall be usable by novice users
questions.e: Functional requirements describe what the system should do. "Generate a daily report" is a functional requirement. The others are non-functional (performance, availability, usability).

questions.q: (2 points) Non-functional requirements can be classified into three types. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.e: Non-functional requirements are classified into Product requirements (system behavior), Organizational requirements (policies/procedures), and External requirements (regulatory/legislative). Implementation requirements is not a category.

questions.q: (2 points) Which requirements elicitation technique involves watching people do their job?
questions.e: Ethnography is an observational technique where the analyst immerses themselves in the working environment to understand how people actually do their work.

questions.q: (2 points) What is a user story in agile development?
o: A real-life example of how a system can be used
A biography of the end user
questions.e: User stories and scenarios are real-life examples of how a system can be used, helping stakeholders relate to and comment on requirements.

questions.q: (2 points) Which validation check ensures that a requirement clearly describes the functions needed?
questions.e: Validity checks ensure the requirement describes functions that best support the customer's needs.

questions.q: (2 points) Requirements management is important because:
o: New requirements emerge and existing ones change during development
It eliminates the need for testing
questions.e: Requirements management is essential because new requirements emerge and existing ones change during development and after the system goes into use.

questions.q: (2 points) What is the primary purpose of system modeling?
o: To develop abstract models presenting different views of the system
To eliminate the need for requirements
questions.e: System modeling develops abstract models that present different views or perspectives of a system, helping understand functionality and communicate with customers.

questions.q: (2 points) Which UML diagram shows the interactions between actors and the system?
questions.e: Use case diagrams show the interactions between actors (external entities) and the system, representing discrete tasks.

questions.q: (2 points) A sequence diagram shows:
o: The sequence of interactions over time
The flow of activities in a process
The state transitions of an object
questions.e: Sequence diagrams show the sequence of interactions between actors and objects over time, typically for a particular use case.

questions.q: (2 points) In a class diagram, what does a filled diamond represent?
questions.e: A filled (black) diamond represents Composition - a strong ownership relationship where the part cannot exist without the whole. An empty diamond represents Aggregation.

questions.q: (2 points) What is the difference between aggregation and composition?
o: In composition, the part cannot exist without the whole; in aggregation, it can
Composition is only used for inheritance
questions.e: In Composition, when the whole is deleted, all parts are deleted (strong ownership). In Aggregation, the part can exist independently of the whole (weak ownership).

questions.q: (2 points) In a use case diagram, what does the <> relationship indicate?
o: The source use case always includes the behavior of the target use case
questions.e: The <<include>> relationship means the source use case always includes the behavior defined in the target use case as part of its normal flow.

questions.q: (2 points) Activity diagrams are used to model:
o: The flow of activities in a process or workflow
questions.e: Activity diagrams show the flow of activities in a process or workflow, including decision points, parallel activities, and transitions.

questions.q: (2 points) What is the purpose of a context model?
o: To show the internal structure of the system
To illustrate the operational context and what lies outside system boundaries
questions.e: Context models illustrate what lies outside the system boundaries and show the operational context - the other systems in the environment.

questions.q: (2 points) In a sequence diagram, what represents an object or participant?
o: Rectangle at the top with a dotted vertical line (lifeline)
questions.e: In sequence diagrams, objects/participants are represented by rectangles at the top with dotted vertical lines (lifelines) extending downward.

questions.q: (2 points) State diagrams (state machines) are used to model:
o: The static structure of a system
How a class responds to events and changes state over time
questions.e: State diagrams model the dynamic behavior of a class - how it responds to events and transitions between states over time.

questions.q: (2 points) In a state diagram, what represents the initial state?
questions.e: The initial state in a state diagram is represented by a filled black circle. The final state is a filled circle within a circle.

questions.q: (2 points) What is a "swimlane" in an activity diagram?
o: A way to group activities performed by the same actor or in a single thread
The final state of the diagram
questions.e: Swimlanes partition an activity diagram to group activities performed by the same actor or within a single thread, showing responsibilities.

questions.q: (1 point) User requirements should be written in technical language so developers can understand them.
questions.e: FALSE: User requirements should be written in natural language that end-users and customers can understand, NOT technical language. System requirements are more technical.

questions.q: (1 point) Ethnography is effective for understanding existing processes but cannot identify new features.
questions.e: TRUE: Ethnography is effective for understanding existing processes but generally cannot identify new features that should be added to a system.

questions.q: (1 point) In a class diagram, an empty diamond represents composition.
questions.e: FALSE: An empty (hollow) diamond represents Aggregation. A filled (black) diamond represents Composition.

questions.q: (1 point) The <> relationship in use cases is used for optional or exceptional behavior.
questions.e: TRUE: The <<extend>> relationship indicates optional or exceptional behavior that enhances the base use case under certain conditions.

questions.q: (1 point) Requirements validation should only be done after the system is implemented.
questions.e: FALSE: Requirements validation should be done BEFORE implementation to catch errors early. Fixing requirements errors after delivery can cost 100x more than fixing implementation errors.

questions.q: (1 point) A scenario is a structured form of a user story that includes starting situation, flow of events, and ending state.
questions.e: TRUE: A scenario is a structured form of user story that includes: starting situation, normal flow of events, what can go wrong, other concurrent activities, and ending state.

questions.q: (3 points) Select ALL that are generic activities in the requirements engineering process:
questions.e: The generic activities in requirements engineering are: Elicitation (discovering requirements), Specification (documenting requirements), Validation (checking requirements), and Management (handling changes). Implementation is NOT part of requirements engineering - it's part of development.

questions.q: (3 points) Select ALL system perspectives that models can represent:
questions.e: The four system perspectives are: External (context/environment), Interaction (between system and environment/components), Structural (organization/data structure), and Behavioral (dynamic behavior/response to events). Financial is not a modeling perspective.

questions.q: What is Software Construction?
o: Only writing code in high-level programming languages
Detailed creation of working software through coding, verification, unit testing, integration testing, and debugging
Only the testing phase of development
questions.e: Software Construction is defined as detailed creation of working, meaningful software through a combination of coding, verification, unit testing, integration testing, and debugging.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the fundamentals of software construction?
questions.e: The fundamentals include: minimizing complexity, anticipating change, constructing for verification, and standards in construction. Maximizing code length is not a goal.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of minimizing complexity in software construction?
o: To reduce the number of developers needed
To create code that is simple and readable
To eliminate all comments from code
questions.e: Minimizing complexity is one of the strongest drivers in software construction. It is achieved by emphasizing code creation that is simple and readable.

questions.q: Anticipation of change affects software construction in several ways. Which of the following is NOT mentioned as affected by anticipating change?
questions.e: Anticipation of change affects: use of control structures, handling of errors, source code organization, code documentation, and coding standards. Marketing is not part of construction.

questions.q: What are the two facets of software reuse?
o: Construction for reuse and Construction with reuse
Testing for reuse and Debugging with reuse
Design for reuse and Implementation with reuse
Planning for reuse and Executing with reuse
questions.e: Reuse has two closely related facets: Construction for reuse (create reusable software assets) and Construction with reuse (reuse software assets in construction).

questions.q: What is Unit Testing?
o: Testing the entire system at once
Testing individual units or components to validate that each performs as expected
questions.e: Unit Testing is testing where individual units or components are tested. The purpose is to validate that each unit of software code performs as expected. A unit is the smallest testable portion.

questions.q: What is the difference between Code Walkthrough and Code Inspection?
o: Walkthrough is semi-formal with author as presenter; Inspection is formal with moderator leading
Walkthrough is for testing; Inspection is for documentation
Inspection happens before coding; Walkthrough after
questions.e: Walkthrough is semi-formal, author is presenter, led by author, reviewers not aware. Inspection is formal, author not presenter, led by moderator, reviewers are aware and well prepared.

questions.q: What is Integration Testing?
o: Combining software modules and testing them as a group to check data flow between modules
questions.e: Integration Testing involves combining different software modules and testing them as a group. It focuses on checking data flow from one module to another.

questions.q: Which integration testing approach tests from top to down following the control flow?
questions.e: Top-down Integration takes place from top to down following the control flow. It uses stubs for testing and allows early prototyping, but needs many stubs.

questions.q: What is Test-driven Development (TDD)?
o: Writing tests first, then writing code to pass those tests
Testing only at the end of development
questions.e: In test-driven development, developers write tests first before writing code. This helps clarify what the code should actually do. An automated unit test framework runs tests after every code contribution.

questions.q: What is refactoring in Extreme Programming?
o: Removing all tests from the code
Improving the structure, readability, efficiency and security of a program
Adding new features to the system
questions.e: Refactoring means improving the structure, readability, efficiency and security of a program. Developers refactor code as soon as potential improvements are found to keep code simple and maintainable.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an Extreme Programming (XP) practice?
questions.e: XP practices include on-site customer (not off-site), pair programming, sustainable pace, small releases, test-first development, refactoring, continuous integration, and others.

questions.q: What is the purpose of using standards in construction?
o: To achieve project objectives for efficiency, quality, and cost
questions.e: Applying external or internal development standards during construction helps achieve a project's objectives for efficiency, quality, and cost. This includes restricting complex language structures.

questions.q: What is Open Source Software?
o: Software that is always free of charge
Software released under a license granting rights to use, change, and distribute the software and source code
questions.e: Open source software is released under a license where the copyright holder grants users the right to use, change, and distribute the software and its source code to anyone for any purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following is part of internal code documentation?
o: Header comment blocks and meaningful variable names
questions.e: Internal documentation includes: header comment blocks, meaningful variable names, program comments, and formatting. External documentation includes: problem description, algorithm description, and data description.

questions.q: Why is skipping unit testing considered a myth in terms of saving time?
o: Because it leads to higher defect fixing costs during later testing phases
Because unit testing takes too long
Because it only benefits small projects
questions.e: Skipping unit testing leads to higher defect fixing costs during System Testing, Integration Testing and Beta Testing. Proper unit tests help fix bugs early and save time and money.

questions.q: What is defect testing in software testing?
o: Testing that proves the system works correctly
Finding inputs in the set that reveal problems with the system
questions.e: The priority in defect testing is to find those inputs in the set that reveal problems with the system. These inputs cause anomalous behavior and outputs that reveal the presence of defects.

questions.q: Why is Integration Testing necessary?
o: Because individual developers may have different programming logic and modules need to work in unity
Because unit testing is not sufficient by itself
questions.e: Integration testing is necessary because modules designed by different developers may have different logic and need to work together. Also, interfaces with databases, hardware, and exception handling could be erroneous.

questions.q: What are construction activities shown in the software development lifecycle?
o: Coding & Debugging, Unit Testing, Integration, and Integration Testing
questions.e: Construction activities include: Coding & Debugging (appears twice), Unit Testing, Integration, and Integration Testing. These fall between detailed design and system testing.

questions.q: What makes code inspection more effective according to the material?
o: The preparation level and team's familiarity with the product
questions.e: The preparation level, not team size, determines inspection effectiveness. The team's effectiveness and efficiency depend on their familiarity with their product.

questions.q: What does the ACM/IEEE Code of Ethics emphasize for software engineers?
o: Making software development a beneficial and respected profession committed to public welfare
Working as fast as possible regardless of quality
questions.e: Software engineers should commit to making analysis, specification, design, development, testing and maintenance a beneficial and respected profession committed to health, safety, and welfare of the public.

questions.q: What benefit does software reuse provide?
o: Quicker development, fewer risks, lower costs, and improved reliability
questions.e: Reuse enables developing new systems more quickly, with fewer development risks and lower costs. It also improves software reliability.

questions.q: What does "anticipating change" mean in software construction?
o: Avoiding any changes to the software
Building extensible software that can be enhanced without disrupting the underlying structure
Waiting for changes to occur before acting
questions.e: Anticipating change means building extensible software that can be enhanced without disrupting the underlying structure. It's supported by specific coding techniques.

questions.q: In Top-down Integration testing, what is used to simulate lower-level modules that haven't been integrated yet?
questions.e: Top-down integration takes help of stubs for testing. Stubs are temporary substitute modules that simulate the behavior of lower-level modules not yet integrated.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of proper unit testing?
o: It eliminates the need for integration testing
It helps fix bugs early, saves time and money, and serves as project documentation
questions.e: Proper unit tests help fix bugs early in the development cycle, save time and money, help developers understand the code base, serve as project documentation, and help with code reuse.

questions.q: What is Black-Box Testing?
o: Testing based on internal code structure and implementation details
Testing functionality without looking at internal code structure, based entirely on requirements
questions.e: Black-box testing is testing functionality without looking at the internal code structure, implementation details, or internal paths. It focuses on inputs and outputs based on requirements.

questions.q: What is the main focus of Black-Box Testing?
questions.e: The main focus of black-box testing is on the validation of functional requirements. It provides abstraction from code and focuses on software system behavior.

questions.q: What is White-Box Testing?
o: Testing without knowledge of internal code
Testing that validates internal structure and working of software code
questions.e: White-box testing validates the internal structure and working of software code. It requires knowledge of the underlying programming language and checks all paths a program can execute.

questions.q: Which black-box testing technique is used to minimize test cases while maintaining reasonable test coverage?
questions.e: Equivalence Class Testing is used to minimize the number of possible test cases to an optimum level while maintaining reasonable test coverage.

questions.q: What is Boundary Value Testing focused on?
o: Testing values at boundaries to determine if ranges are acceptable
questions.e: Boundary Value Testing is focused on the values at boundaries. It determines whether a certain range of values are acceptable by the system, useful for reducing test cases.

questions.q: What is Cyclomatic Complexity?
o: The number of lines of code in a program
A software metric used to measure the paths complexity and independent paths in source code
The number of functions in a program
The execution time of a program
questions.e: Cyclomatic Complexity is a software metric used to measure the paths complexity of a program. It's a quantitative measure of independent paths in the source code.

questions.q: What is an independent path in Cyclomatic Complexity?
o: A path that visits all nodes
A path that has at least one edge which has not been traversed before in any other paths
A path without any decision nodes
questions.e: An independent path is defined as a path that has at least one edge which has not been traversed before in any other paths.

questions.q: How is Cyclomatic Complexity calculated using edges and nodes?
questions.e: Cyclomatic Complexity is calculated as V(G) = E - N + 2, where E is the number of edges and N is the number of nodes. Alternatively, V(G) = P + 1, where P is the number of predicates/decision nodes.

questions.q: What is the alternative formula for Cyclomatic Complexity using predicates?
questions.e: Cyclomatic Complexity can also be calculated as V(G) = P + 1, where P is the number of predicates (decision nodes) in the control flow graph.

questions.q: What is Basis Path Testing?
o: Testing only the main execution path
Execution of all possible blocks with maximum path coverage using the least number of test cases
questions.e: Basis Path Testing involves execution of all possible blocks in a program and achieves maximum path coverage with the least number of test cases. The number of test cases equals the cyclomatic complexity.

questions.q: What does Verification mean in V&V (Verification and Validation)?
o: Are we building the right product?
Are we building the product right?
questions.e: Verification asks "Are we building the product right?" It aims to check that the software meets its stated functional and non-functional requirements.

questions.q: What does Validation mean in V&V (Verification and Validation)?
o: Are we building the product right?
Are we building the right product?
questions.e: Validation asks "Are we building the right product?" It's a more general process aimed at ensuring the software meets the customer's expectations.

questions.q: What are the four levels of testing?
questions.e: The four levels of testing are: Unit Testing (test individual components), Integration Testing (test integrated components), System Testing (test entire system), and Acceptance Testing (test final system).

questions.q: What is Acceptance Testing?
o: Beta testing done by actual end users to verify requirements are met
questions.e: Acceptance testing is beta testing done by actual end users. It's conducted to find if requirements of a specification are met. Only black-box testing techniques are used.

questions.q: What is Regression Testing?
o: Testing done after code fixes or upgrades to check new code hasn't affected existing code
questions.e: Regression Testing is done after code fixes, upgrades, or system maintenance to check that the new code has not affected the existing code. The product must be tested against previous test cases.

questions.q: What advantage does White-Box Testing have over Black-Box Testing?
o: It can be done before coding
It tests internal details of code and checks all paths a program can execute
questions.e: White-box testing tests the internal details of the code and checks all paths that a program can execute. However, it requires waiting until after designing and coding to select test cases.

questions.q: What is an advantage of Black-Box Testing?
o: Test case selection can be done before implementation
questions.e: Black-box testing allows test case selection to be done before the implementation of a program, and helps in getting the design and coding correct with respect to the specification.

questions.q: How many test cases are needed in Basis Path Testing?
o: Equal to the number of lines of code
Equal to the cyclomatic complexity of the program
Equal to the number of functions
Twice the number of decision nodes
questions.e: The number of test cases in Basis Path Testing will be equal to the cyclomatic complexity of the program. It guarantees to execute each statement at least once.

questions.q: Which type of testing is NOT related to testing specific functionality but rather non-functional requirements?
questions.e: Non-functional testing is not related to testing specific functionality, but rather non-functional requirements such as performance, scalability, and usability.

questions.q: What does Decision Table Testing involve?
o: Putting causes and their effects in a matrix with unique combinations in each column
questions.e: Decision Table Testing puts causes and their effects in a matrix. There is a unique combination in each column, allowing systematic testing of different combinations.

questions.q: What is the first step in performing Black-Box Testing?
o: Examine the requirements and specifications of the system
questions.e: The first step in Black-Box Testing is to examine the requirements and specifications of the system. Then testers choose valid/invalid inputs, determine expected outputs, construct test cases, execute them, and compare results.

questions.q: What is the purpose of using Cyclomatic Complexity in testing?
o: To determine independent path executions and improve code coverage
To count the number of bugs
questions.e: Cyclomatic Complexity helps determine independent path executions, assures all paths are tested at least once, helps focus on uncovered paths, improves code coverage, evaluates risk, and reduces project failure risks.

questions.q: What is the difference between Black-Box and White-Box Testing regarding module communication?
o: Black-box facilitates testing communication amongst modules; White-box does not
White-box facilitates testing communication amongst modules; Black-box does not
questions.e: Black-box testing facilitates testing communication amongst modules, while white-box testing does not facilitate testing communication amongst modules (it focuses on internal code paths).

questions.q: What are the steps for Basis Path Testing?
o: Write code, test code, fix bugs
Draw control graph, calculate cyclomatic complexity, identify basis set, generate test cases
questions.e: Steps are: 1) Draw control graph from source code, 2) Calculate Cyclomatic Complexity using V(G) = E - N + 2 or V(G) = P + 1, 3) Identify basis set of paths, 4) Generate test cases to execute all paths.

questions.q: What is Defect Testing focused on?
o: Finding inputs that reveal problems with the system
questions.e: The priority in defect testing is to find those inputs that reveal problems with the system. These inputs cause anomalous behavior and outputs that reveal the presence of defects.

questions.q: It is practically possible to derive a complete set of stable software requirements in a changing environment.
questions.e: Requirements change frequently in modern environments, making it impractical to derive a complete stable set.

questions.q: In generic products, the specification of what the software should do is owned by the customer of the software and they make decisions on required software changes.
questions.e: In generic products, the specification is owned by the software developer, not the customer.

questions.q: In the Unified Process model, requirements are determined iteratively and may span more than one phase of the process.
questions.e: The Unified Process is iterative and requirements are refined across multiple phases.

questions.q: The Incremental model combines the elements of linear and parallel process flow.
questions.e: The Incremental model does combine linear progression with parallel development of increments.

questions.q: Scaling up is concerned with using agile methods for large systems that cannot be developed by a small team.
questions.e: Scaling agile methods for large, complex systems is indeed a significant challenge.

questions.q: What is the primary focus of software engineering?
questions.e: Software engineering focuses on all aspects of software production from specification to maintenance.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT considered an attribute of good software?
questions.e: Good software should be predictable and reliable. Unpredictability is a negative attribute.

questions.q: What percentage of software costs are typically attributed to development?
questions.e: Roughly 60% of software costs are development costs, 40% are testing costs.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes customized products in software engineering?
o: Software developed for mass market distribution
Free software available for public use
Software commissioned by a specific customer to meet their needs
questions.e: Customized products are commissioned by specific customers for their particular needs.

questions.q: What is one of the key challenges faced by software engineering?
o: Coping with increasing diversity in systems
questions.e: Software engineers must cope with increasing diversity, reduced delivery times, and developing trustworthy software.

questions.q: Which principle is NOT part of professional ethical responsibilities in software engineering?
questions.e: Professional ethics prioritize honesty, competence, and confidentiality over pure profit maximization.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the main activities in a software process?
questions.e: The fundamental software engineering activities are specification, development, validation, and evolution.

questions.q: Define a software process and list its four fundamental activities.
questions.m: A software process is a structured set of activities required to develop a software system. The four fundamental activities are: (1) Software specification - defining what the system should do; (2) Software development - designing and implementing the system; (3) Software validation - checking that it does what the customer wants; (4) Software evolution - changing the system in response to changing customer needs.

questions.q: ___________An iterative model. It enables you to develop increasingly more complete version of the software. Emphasis on risk management.
questions.e: Evolutionary/Spiral model is iterative, enables increasingly complete versions, and emphasizes risk management.

questions.q: User requirements are expressed as Scenarios in Extreme Programming.
questions.e: False. User requirements are expressed as User Stories (not scenarios) in Extreme Programming.

questions.q: The incremental model of software development is:
o: A reasonable approach when requirements are well defined
A good approach when a working core product is required quickly
The best approach to use for project with large development teams
questions.e: All statements are correct. Incremental model is reasonable for well-defined requirements, good for quick core product delivery, and suitable for large teams.

questions.q: CMM model is used to ____.
questions.e: CMM (Capability Maturity Model) is used to improve the software process by assessing and improving organizational processes.

questions.q: In risk planning the term risk avoidance refers to:
o: Reducing the probability that the risk will arise
Putting a contingency plan to deal with the risk
questions.e: Risk avoidance specifically refers to reducing the probability that the risk will arise. Other options refer to risk mitigation and contingency planning.

questions.q: Requirements change is a:
questions.e: Requirements change can be both a project risk (affects schedule/cost) and a product risk (affects functionality/quality).

questions.q: Consider a system where a heat sensor detects an intrusion and alerts the security company. What kind of requirement is the system providing?
questions.e: This is a functional requirement because it describes a specific behavior/function: detecting intrusion and alerting.

questions.q: For which of the following reasons is the waterfall model not suitable?
questions.e: Waterfall model's main drawback is difficulty accommodating changes. It requires well-understood, stable requirements.

questions.q: Which of the following defines the degree of intra-dependability within elements of a module?
questions.e: Cohesion is an intra-module concept measuring how closely related elements within a module are.

questions.q: Which of the following is a MAIN purpose of a Sprint Backlog?
o: For the Developers to manage themselves during the Sprint
For the Scrum Master to manage the progress during the Sprint
For the Developers to manage the number of hours spent on tasks in the Sprint
For the Product Owner to understand what the Developers has committed to for a Sprint
questions.e: The Sprint Backlog is primarily for Developers to manage themselves during the Sprint (self-organization).

questions.q: What are the different levels of Testing?
questions.e: All are levels of testing: Unit, Integration, System, and Acceptance testing.

questions.q: In the maintenance phase the product must be tested against previous test cases. This is known as _________ testing.
questions.e: Regression testing ensures that changes haven't adversely affected existing functionality by re-running previous test cases.

questions.q: When your system accepts a batch of data and then applies a series of sequential transformations to it, the best fit architecture will be:
questions.e: Pipe & Filter architecture is designed for batch sequential processing with data transformations.

questions.q: A good software design should exhibit several attributes, one of them is Commodity, this means:
o: A program should not have any bugs that inhibit its function
A program should be suitable for the purposes for which it was intended
The experience of using the program should be pleasurable
A program should not have any inconsistencies, or omissions
questions.e: Commodity means the program should be suitable for its intended purposes.

questions.q: Risks can be classified to:
questions.e: Risks are typically classified into Project risks, People risks, and Business risks.

questions.q: One of the following is not considered as Extreme programming practice:
questions.e: XP requires "On-site customer" not "Off-site customer." The customer should be available to the team.

questions.q: Design and implementation processes are concerned with transforming a requirements specification into an executable software system:
questions.e: True. Design and implementation transform requirements specifications into working software systems.

questions.q: Agile methods work well in cases where the software is tightly integrated with other systems rather than being stand-alone systems.
questions.e: False. Agile methods work better for stand-alone systems. Tightly integrated systems require more upfront design and coordination.

questions.q: Non-functional requirements often constrain the system being developed and the development process being used.
questions.e: True. Non-functional requirements (performance, security, etc.) constrain both the system design and the development process.

questions.q: Which model is "use-case driven, architecture-centric, iterative and incremental"?
questions.e: Unified Process (UP) is characterized as use-case driven, architecture-centric, iterative and incremental.

questions.q: Which model is best for a well understood problem with minimal or no changes in the requirements?
questions.e: Waterfall model is best when requirements are well-understood and stable with minimal changes expected.

questions.q: Which model uses a cyclic approach for incrementally growing a system's degree of definition and implementation while decreasing its degree of risk?
questions.e: Spiral Model is characterized by its cyclic, risk-driven approach with increasing definition and decreasing risk.

questions.q: Which model is best when requirements are huge and unclear and needs user involvement?
questions.e: Prototype model is best for unclear requirements as it allows stakeholders to provide feedback and refine requirements iteratively.

questions.q: Which model is best when there is a compelling need to provide a limited set of software functionality to users quickly?
questions.e: Incremental model delivers working software in increments, allowing quick delivery of core functionality.

questions.q: What is the main characteristic of the Waterfall model?
o: Plan-driven with separate and distinct phases
questions.e: Waterfall is a plan-driven model with separate and distinct phases of specification and development.

questions.q: What does the Incremental Model focus on?
o: Delivery of operational product with each increment
questions.e: Incremental model focuses on delivering an operational product with each increment, with highest priority requirements in early increments.

questions.q: In Scrum, what is the typical duration of a Sprint?
questions.e: Sprints in Scrum are timeboxed iterations, typically lasting 1-4 weeks.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the Product Backlog in Scrum?
questions.e: The Product Owner is responsible for managing and prioritizing the Product Backlog.

questions.q: What is the role of the Scrum Master?
o: Managing the team's tasks and assignments
Facilitating Scrum process and removing impediments
questions.e: Scrum Master facilitates the Scrum process, coaches the team, and removes impediments.

questions.q: Which XP practice involves writing tests before writing code?
questions.e: Test-Driven Development (TDD) requires writing tests first to clarify what the code should do.

questions.q: What does Refactoring mean in Extreme Programming?
o: Improving code structure, readability, efficiency without changing functionality
questions.e: Refactoring improves structure, readability, efficiency, and security without changing functionality.

questions.q: What is Verification in V&V?
o: Are we building the right product?
Are we building the product right?
questions.e: Verification asks "Are we building the product right?" - checking against requirements.

questions.q: What is Validation in V&V?
o: Are we building the product right?
Are we building the right product?
questions.e: Validation asks "Are we building the right product?" - ensuring customer expectations are met.

questions.q: What is the formula for Cyclomatic Complexity using edges and nodes?
questions.e: Cyclomatic Complexity is calculated as V(G) = E - N + 2, where E is edges and N is nodes.

questions.q: What does high coupling mean?
questions.e: High coupling means modules are highly interdependent, which is undesirable. We want low coupling and high cohesion.

questions.q: What is Black-Box Testing focused on?
o: Functional requirements without looking at code
questions.e: Black-box testing validates functional requirements without looking at internal code structure.

questions.q: Which testing level tests the entire system?
questions.e: System Testing tests the entire integrated system to verify it meets requirements.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Integration Testing?
o: Test combined modules to check interactions and data flow
questions.e: Integration Testing combines modules and tests them as a group to verify interactions and data flow between modules.

questions.q: Who typically performs Acceptance Testing?
questions.e: Acceptance Testing (beta testing) is done by actual end users or customers to verify requirements are met.
